newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors seek union arrest warrants.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors seek union arrest warrants.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors said on Thursday they are seeking arrest warrants for leaders of a militant union body organising nationwide strikes.
The head of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions had earlier threatened all-out stoppages, including a public sector shutdown, if warrants are issued.
"We are seeking arrest warrants for seven union leaders this morning," Shin Kun-soo, senior prosecutor at the Seoul Prosecution Office, told Reuters.
The seven included confederation president Kwon Young-kil, who is commanding the strikes from a makeshift tent on the snow-covered ground of Seoul's Myongdong catholic church.
"Even if we have arrest warrants, we will still need to talk to officials at Myongdong Cathedral for the church's cooperation for the arrest," Shin said.

The confederation claimed more than 200,000 members were on strike, including more than 50,000 car workers, in protest at a controversial labour bill pushed through parliament on December 26 which, among other things, allows worker layoffs.
